## Mammals Sleep data 
__Q1.__ Use filter() to subset msleep to only animals who are awake for at least 12 hours of the day.
```{r}
Awake <- msleep |> 
 filter(awake >= 12) |> 
  arrange(awake)
Awake
```
__Q2.__ Use mutate() to create a new column called percent_day_awake that gives the percentage of the day that each species spends awake. Use select() with everything() at the end to verify your calculation.
```{r}
day_awake <- msleep |> 
  mutate(percent_day_awake = awake / 24 * 100) |> 
  select(name, percent_day_awake, everything())
day_awake
```
## Storm tracks data
__Q3.__ Use group_by() and summarise() to calculate the number of storms per year.
```{r}
storms_per_year<- storms |> 
  group_by(year) |> 
  summarise(num_storms = n())
storms_per_year
```

__Q4.__ Use filter() to subset storms to only storms with wind speeds greater than 50 knots, then use arrange() to sort by wind descending.
```{r}
storms_speed <- storms |> 
  filter(wind > 50) |> 
  arrange(desc(wind)) |> 
  select(name, wind, everything())
storms_speed
```
## A Comparison of Site Preferences of Two Species of Lizard
__Q5.__ Determine which Site and Diameter combination has the highest total grahami.
```{r, message=FALSE}
Grahami <- lizards |> 
  group_by(Site, Diameter) |> 
  summarise(new_grahami = sum(grahami)) |> 
  arrange(desc(new_grahami))
Grahami
```
